background_propositions.quantifiers: For every rational gamma and each admissible psi, for almost every x in [0,1], infinitely many (a,q) in Z x N satisfy (78), hence infinitely many q satisfy (76).
background_propositions.convergence_scope: If (52) fails, Theorem 14 asserts finitely many adapted-coprime pairs almost everywhere, not convergence of the unrestricted weak norm inequality by simply removing coprimality.
background_propositions.strictness_argument: Apply the theorem to psi/2, whose totient sum still diverges. Outside the countable exact-equality set E_gamma={(a+gamma)/q}, solutions require psi(q)>0, and 0<||qx-gamma||<=|qx-gamma-a|<=psi(q)/2<psi(q). Each fixed q permits finitely many a, so infinitely many pairs give infinitely many denominators.
background_propositions.decisive_match: The actual gcd is gcd(A+aB,q), not gcd(a,q); source <= is preserved and the strict consequence is justified by scaling, including zeros of psi.

background_propositions.shift: For each such f, an explicitly constructible Liouville gamma depending only on f, fixed before and independently of psi.
background_propositions.approximation_functions: Nonnegative approximation functions psi; no monotonicity of psi is imposed.
background_propositions.log_notation: Literal source Log notation retained; no different logarithm convention substituted.
background_propositions.quantifier_order: For every monotone f tending to infinity, there exists an explicitly constructible Liouville gamma(f), such that for every psi satisfying either displayed condition, for almost every x in R there are infinitely many q satisfying ||qx-gamma||<=psi(q).
background_propositions.null_set_qualification: The exceptional null set may depend on psi; no common full-measure set for all psi is asserted.
background_propositions.strictness_argument: For the same f and its same gamma, replacing psi by psi/2 halves either positive liminf. Removing E_gamma then gives the strict weak inequality.
background_propositions.decisive_match: Both archived lower bounds match the primary theorem: positive normalized liminf, power 1+epsilon with phi(q)/q in (88), versus power 2+epsilon without phi(q)/q in the alternative.
